predecessors.name: Uyunid Emirate
predecessors.text: the Uyunid emirate of al-Ahsa and Qatif, whose 'successors' the Usfurids 'eventually overthrew'

successors.name: Portuguese Empire
successors.text: the Awal Islands, taken in 1521 from Muqrin ibn Zamil

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Al-Ahsa and Qatif, which 'came under the sovereignty of the Ottoman Empire' in 1550

ledger.x: 1392: the seat moves from al-Ahsa to Qatif.
1521: Jabrid rule ends on the Bahrain islands and the state is closed.

wars.name: Usfurid victory over the Mongols at Basra
wars.outcome: The Usfurid forces 'defeated the Mongols' at Basra in 1354; no land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Jabrid-Hormuz tribute dispute
wars.outcome: The Jabrids retook the Bahrain islands from the princes of Hormuz (undated, Al-Ahsa page); the Jabrid king Muqrin ibn Zamil 'had refused to pay the tribute Hormuz demanded' (Hormuz page); the Jabrid ruler 'was nominally a vassal of Hormuz'.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Bahrain
wars.outcome: The Portuguese conquered the Awal Islands in 1521 from Muqrin ibn Zamil, ending Jabrid rule of the archipelago.

certainty.note: No survey lines: the Gulf-coast shape (Kuwait to the northern UAE, Qatar) and the desert frontier towards Najd are approximate, and the pages opened give no extent beyond 'Eastern Arabia'.
